topics.title: Executive summary
text: AMReye.AI APEX XR is the top-of-the-line clinical + research + bio-automation configuration of the AMReye.AI platform. It is conceived as a modular benchtop workstation, not a compact first product. Its purpose is to unite standardized plate imaging, direct broth microdilution, controlled incubation, research phenomics, multimodal sensing, plate and liquid handling, traceable data management and laboratory orchestration in one system.

topics.title: What the flagship is - and is not
text: It is the eventual maximum configuration that demonstrates the full AMReye.AI platform architecture.

topics.title: Positioning
text: AMReye.AI should be positioned as an AMR/AST-first modular microbiology platform that can expand into research and laboratory automation. It should not be positioned as the only AI plate-imaging system: established products already validate smart incubation, digital imaging, AI plate analysis, automated ID/AST and full laboratory automation [S16-S19].

topics.title: Why a flagship is necessary
text: Architecture proof: demonstrates how optics, biology, safety, AI, robotics and records fit into one coherent system.

topics.title: Current PoC, proposed flagship and future R&D
text: This maturity map is intentionally conservative. The accessible project sources document a compact, phone/controlled-imaging AST concept and a much broader aspirational architecture, but they do not constitute evidence that the flagship has been integrated or clinically validated [S1-S5].

topics.title: Full flagship architecture
text: APEX XR is organized across three physical zones, four compute/software layers and two optical paths. This separation prevents heat and operating-system faults from becoming biological-control failures and prevents one camera from being forced to compromise between metrology and phenomics.

topics.title: Data and control flow
text: Every transition is logged in the Plate Information Management System (PIMS). Raw data are retained with hashes, timestamps, calibration identifiers, software/model versions and user actions so a result can be reconstructed.

topics.title: Updated flagship hardware stack
text: Named components are reference classes for an engineering build. Production selection must also consider lifecycle, regional availability, environmental ratings, serviceability, EMC, calibration, supplier qualification and regulatory evidence.

topics.title: Jetson AGX Thor / T5000 rationale
text: The Jetson AGX Thor developer kit combines a T5000 system-on-module, Blackwell GPU, 128 GB memory and up to 2070 FP4 TFLOPS within a 40-130 W operating envelope. NVIDIA positions the developer kit for development and testing; production devices should use a production module and a qualified or custom carrier [S6-S7].

topics.title: Four software layers and BAHU/SaaS architecture
BAHU - Bio-Automation & Human User Interface
text: BAHU is the local operating and orchestration layer beneath the AMReye.AI brand. It gives one human-facing interface to AST, MIC, incubation, imaging, gas control, robotics, liquid handling, QC, research protocols and instrument integrations.

topics.title: SaaS / Hive services
text: Fleet health, calibration status, software distribution and device configuration governance.

topics.title: PIMS and the digital twin
text: PIMS - the Plate Information Management System - creates a physical-sample-to-digital-record chain. One record should include sample and plate identifiers, organism or assay metadata, media, antibiotic/panel map, lots, inoculum, operator, timestamps, environmental history, every image, derived measurements, QC, standards version, model version, manual edits and final disposition.

topics.title: CLSI/EUCAST structured standards engine
text: Breakpoints and interpretive rules must be represented as a licensed, version-controlled structured database. CLSI and EUCAST update rules and QC information; EUCAST publishes current clinical and RAST-specific tables, while CLSI emphasizes use of current standards and method-specific procedures [S12-S14].

topics.title: LIMS/LIS/HIS and OEM integration
text: Order and result interfaces through laboratory-approved standards and profiles (for example HL7 v2 messaging, FHIR where appropriate, CSV/SFTP for bounded legacy workflows, and vendor APIs).

topics.title: Offline and edge operation
text: Core run control, image capture, measurement, locally installed standards rules, review and report generation remain available without internet. Data are queued for encrypted synchronization after connectivity returns. The system must visibly show synchronization state and prevent conflicting rule/model updates from being applied mid-run.

topics.title: Cybersecurity and software lifecycle
text: Secure boot where supported, signed software/model/rules packages, encrypted storage and TLS for external interfaces.

topics.title: Intended clinical capability set
text: Calibrated disk-diffusion plate imaging and zone-of-inhibition measurement.

topics.title: Research capability set
text: Time-lapse RGB phenomics and colony growth kinetics.

topics.title: Use Cases - What It Does, Who Uses It, and Why It Matters
text: This chapter is the operational center of the dossier. Each use case identifies the customer, problem, modules, workflow, output, value, maturity and evidence boundary. APEX XR can host all of these modules, but not every customer needs every module and not every capability is clinical.

topics.title: Heteroresistance and satellite-colony research
text: Research has shown that resistant subpopulations can be unstable and difficult to detect. An inner colony or irregular zone should prompt expert review and suitable confirmatory investigation; an image flag alone does not prove heteroresistance. Population analysis profiling was used in the cited study. [S26]

topics.title: Competitor and benchmark context
text: APEX XR should be presented as a differentiated product strategy, not as a claim that no comparable capabilities exist. The market already demonstrates digital incubation, AI image analysis, quantitative AST and full laboratory automation.

topics.title: Competitive claim rules
text: Describe competitor capabilities accurately and from current primary sources.

topics.title: Why the flagship price differs from Lite/Core/Clinical
text: Two high-performance imaging paths instead of one compact capture module.

topics.title: Regulatory statement
text: The intended clinical configuration is expected to fall within India's IVD regulatory framework. CDSCO states that IVD manufacture/import/clinical performance/sale are governed by the Medical Devices Rules, 2017, and classification depends on intended purpose and risk [S20]. A current CDSCO list includes an identification and antibiotic-susceptibility analyser entry, but the final classification of AMReye.AI - including software, accessories, claims and combined configurations - must be formally determined with regulatory counsel and the competent authority. The older project assertion of a fixed 'Class B' pathway should not be repeated as fact.

topics.title: Claims that must not appear without evidence
text: Sub-micron whole-plate measurement accuracy.

topics.title: Appendix A. Detailed flagship BOM categories and pricing assumptions
text: The planning allocation below reconciles to ₹54.96 lakh. It is an engineering model, not a purchase order. It includes prototype integration allowance but excludes GST, recurring software/cloud, salaries, clinical studies, regulatory fees, facility changes, consumables and mass-production tooling unless explicitly noted.

topics.title: A.1 Cost uncertainty and exclusions
text: Foreign exchange, freight, customs duties, distributor margin and supplier minimum order quantities can move the optics/compute cost materially.

topics.title: Appendix B. Critical corrections and design requirements
RTOS and independent embedded control
text: The proposed STM32 control layer runs time-sensitive hardware tasks independently of the operator interface and AI computer. FreeRTOS is an RTOS for microcontrollers; its presence alone does not establish that an AMReye.AI controller is deterministic or safe. The project must define and test its own deadlines, priorities and fault responses. [S21][S22][S24]

topics.title: Watchdogs, interlocks and fault-state recovery
text: A proposed fault model should distinguish startup checks, ready state, active acquisition, paused operation, recoverable faults and a latched safe state. Every transition needs a cause, timestamp and recovery condition. [S21][S22]

topics.title: Multi-plate camera gantry concept
text: The September group discussion describes one camera moving above multiple plates on an interval schedule, with the incubation region centrally located and electronics below. This is a separate research configuration from the earlier single-plate enclosure drawings. [S27][S28]

topics.title: Decontamination concept and UV safety boundaries
text: The group discussion proposes an optional post-run internal UV cycle with interruption when the access door opens. This is an unvalidated decontamination concept. An illuminated chamber is not evidence of effective sterilisation. [S27]

topics.title: Open hardware, software licensing and commercial services
text: The group discussion supports an accessible, buildable hardware pathway and service-based software or AI revenue. Earlier proposals also discuss open hardware and research access. These are intended models, not proof that design files or code have already been released under a licence. [S21][S27]

topics.title: Educational and public-health access model
text: The project aims to improve access for teaching institutions, nonprofit users and resource-constrained laboratories. The group discussion proposes affordability through local construction, modular scope and potential public-health partnerships. [S27]

topics.title: Web app, offline reader and instrument application
text: The public website is the discovery and documentation layer. A browser-based app can present the same content, while an installed instrument application would need controlled releases, local data handling, hardware interfaces and its own validation. [S27]

topics.title: Goa diagnostic capacity and public-spending research framework
text: The team's proposed study asks whether public-health investment supports the diagnostic capacity required for AMR preparedness. It connects microbiology requirements, laboratory availability, public spending and implementation feasibility. This page states a research framework, not the findings of a completed CAG audit. [S27]

topics.title: Bacterial-outbreak preparedness scenarios
text: COVID demonstrates the importance of diagnostic capacity and coordinated information, but AMReye.AI's current AST direction does not diagnose or solve a viral outbreak. The defensible counterfactual concerns future bacterial or AMR events and the availability of validated microbiology infrastructure. [S27]

topics.title: Growth patterns, phenomics and identity limits
text: The original idea began with image-based zone measurement and expanded toward time-resolved observation of bacterial and fungal growth. Imaging can create reproducible phenotypic features, but appearance alone does not establish strain identity, genotype, protein expression or clinical susceptibility. [S21][S22][S27]

topics.title: Model evaluation and dataset governance
text: Treat each model as a separate evidence object: intended task, input format, training provenance, test protocol, performance bounds and review workflow. A plate-segmentation model is not automatically a strain or protein model. [S21]

topics.title: From laboratory records to governed surveillance
text: WHO GLASS provides a framework for AMR surveillance and its data requirements. Any AMReye.AI connection to a national programme would need agreed definitions, laboratory quality processes and responsible reporting. It is not an existing GLASS integration. [S25]

topics.title: Project history and source reconciliation
text: The repository contains multiple generations: the early single-plate image-analysis idea, the three-zone enclosure, the expanded technical manual, the APEX XR flagship dossier and the later multi-plate gantry and public-health discussions. They should remain dated alternatives rather than being silently combined into one manufactured device. [S21][S22][S27][S28]

topics.title: Team roles and responsibilities
text: Current team responsibilities confirmed by Namdev Tukaram Shirodkar on 14 September 2026. These assignments replace earlier team-role summaries in the current project documentation.

topics.title: Validation mode and correction provenance
text: The September master specifies a proposed Validation Mode that compares a reference result with an AMReye.AI measurement. Each record should retain method, organism, antimicrobial, disc potency where relevant, standards version, category comparison, disagreement classification and reviewer decisions. This is a software roadmap requirement, not an existing validated instrument feature. [S29][S31]

topics.title: Unreadable images, review and recapture
text: The proposed pipeline must be able to abstain when image quality, growth, condensation, plate geometry or inhibition-zone boundaries are unsuitable. The master defines NOT READABLE, REVIEW and RECAPTURE outcomes so a system is not forced to produce a measurement or susceptibility call. [S29]

topics.title: Bio-Vault and APEX XR: separate configuration studies
text: The September master describes a proposed three-zone Bio-Vault arrangement with Jetson Orin NX, Raspberry Pi 5 and BME688. The earlier APEX XR dossier explores a larger flagship architecture including Thor/T5000 and BME690. These are alternative configuration studies, not one final bill of materials or a confirmed manufactured instrument. [S29][S21]

topics.title: Reader V1: endpoint disk-diffusion reading
text: The present priority is an endpoint reader: a calibrated plate image, visible zone measurement, quality checks, uncertainty and qualified review. Broader instrument and assay capabilities remain separate proposals.

topics.title: Campus and laboratory audit collaboration
text: A proposed collaboration starts with equipment and workflow mapping, operator interviews, bottlenecks, training, data permissions and a scoped pilot. Agree the owner, deliverables, budget and acceptance criteria before work begins. No campus partnership is claimed as signed.

topics.title: Cell-culture workflow research
text: Explore record keeping, imaging review and workflow traceability for cell culture as a separate research direction. Requirements for cell lines, containment, imaging, quality controls and qualified supervision need independent definition. No automated culture capability is claimed.

topics.title: Stem-cell research workflows
text: Stem-cell work is a future research direction, not a current product capability or therapeutic service. Any collaboration needs an intended research question, appropriate approvals, qualified facilities and independent methods for identity and quality assessment.

topics.title: Organoid and tissue-model research
text: Organoids and tissue models are potential future research contexts. Define the biological model, authorized data, relevant measurements and independent validation before selecting hardware or making performance claims.

topics.title: UTI and urine-culture workflow research
text: A possible application is a bounded urine-culture laboratory workflow with validated plate reading and reviewable AST. It does not imply diagnosis directly from an unprocessed specimen or autonomous treatment advice.

topics.title: MRSA and molecular-result integration
text: Study how authorized results from qualified molecular instruments could complement phenotype records. Real-time PCR and reverse-transcription PCR are different methods; the intended method remains to be specified. No resistance gene is inferred from a plate image.

topics.title: Bioinformatics and phenotype–genotype research
text: Use traceable identifiers and versioned reference resources to study authorized phenotype and molecular data. Keep measured genotypes distinct from image-based hypotheses and computational predictions.

topics.title: Measured, derived, imputed and simulated data
text: Every plate value needs an origin label, unit, timestamp, uncertainty and quality state where applicable. A blank channel stays unavailable. Derived or imputed information must not silently become a direct measurement.

topics.title: Interoperability, APIs and audit trails
text: An interface needs a defined data contract, identity mapping, authorization, version handling and acceptance tests. Standards names and API availability do not mean a working hospital integration exists.

topics.title: System as a Service delivery model
text: Explore equipment access with maintenance, calibration, training and support as a service package. Keep it distinct from the software subscription, and validate customer demand, operating costs and contract terms before offering it commercially.

topics.title: Privacy and access governance
text: Keep public explanations separate from protected technical and partner material. Any real laboratory data would need appropriate rights, permissions, retention rules and a documented governance model before use.

topics.title: Automation vocabulary with practical meaning
text: Digital twin means a traceable record with clearly labelled data origins. Edge AI means processing close to the instrument. Human-in-the-loop means qualified review. Robotics, sensor fusion, multimodal AI, organoids and lab orchestration are research directions unless supported by specific completed evidence.
